note: Medium held-out set (session 5): written AFTER the amortized-loop, product-target and log-factor rules were added, and never used to change any rule. Labels follow what a good interviewer would say, not what the analyzer can detect.

samples.note: Prefix/suffix products written with a separate suffix array.
Divides the total product: wrong as soon as there's a zero (and division is disallowed).
Linear scan: correct, but the problem requires O(log n).
`lo < hi` never examines the last remaining element, so single-element and edge targets are missed.
Largest-coin-first greedy: fails for coins like [9, 6, 5, 1] and amount 11.
Top-down with memoisation: correct and on target.
Classic O(n^2) DP: correct, but O(n log n) exists.
Looks ahead from every day: correct, quadratic.
Monotonic stack implemented with an int array and a top index.
Greedy from the right: track the leftmost index known to reach the end.
Forgets that a single '0' can't be decoded on its own.
Sorts everything: correct, but a size-k heap gives O(n log k).
Every start index, extended with running counts: correct, quadratic.
